not_served.title: Says backfilling the cached offsets is the whole fix
not_served.correct: A cached offset is only right for part of the year, and period boundaries are computed weeks or months ahead (a Nov 2 boundary is computed in October, a Mar 15 one in February), so a fresh offset today is still wrong for a date on the other side of a clock change. boundary() has to use the zone's offset on that date (tz.startOfLocalDay). A backfill is fine as a stopgap for tonight, not as the fix.

not_served.correct: The ticket says the credit rounds DOWN to the cent (its own example: floor(4900 × 13 / 31) = 2054, where Math.round gives 2055).

evaluation.rootCause: customers.js caches utcOffsetMinutes at signup (-240 for New York in summer), and boundary() in subscriptions.js computes every period boundary with that cached offset. After the clocks went back (Europe on Oct 25, the US on Nov 1), boundaries for customers who signed up in summer land an hour early: Nov 2 00:00 in New York was computed as 04:00Z, which is 23:00 on Nov 1. The hourly renewal job renewed and charged those subscriptions at 23:00 local, and the invoice was dated with the customer's real local date (Nov 1). The cancellation check compares the customer's local date with cancelOn ("2026-11-02"), so it only fired at 00:00 local, an hour after the charge: customers who had cancelled were charged for another month. It predates the Oct 30 Chronos move: Berlin customers hit the same thing on Oct 26 (CS-41877, closed as user error). Customers who signed up in winter are correct now and will renew an hour late after the March change.
